findings.detail: The M4-S26-T1 stem describes a PostToolUse hook that rewrites the status codes inside returned tool results. Its option C also says the hook transforms each tool result. Together these tell the examinee that a PostToolUse hook acts only after the tool has run and returned. That is the answer of M4-S19-T1: the PostToolUse hook ran after send_report had already sent the email, so it could not block it. Option D of M4-S26-T1 ('runs on the outgoing call before the fetch tool returns') also points to the timing distinction that M4-S19-T1 tests.
The wrong idea 'raise max_tokens so the output has more room, which fixes the problem' is a wrong option in 4 questions: S18 A, S22 C, S25 D and S30 A. The limit is 2.
